Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with complaints of neck pain and stiffness. The mechansim
of injury is consistent with the reported symptoms, and the presentation is plausible for a crash of this type. Initial examination
revealed reduced cervical range of motion and tenderness over the paraspinal muscles, while neurological screening and imaging
findings were within normal limits. The patient has a remote history of a minor cervical strain that resolved completely without
lasting residual symptoms. Over the course of care, the patient completed 30 visits, which is smoewhat longer than typically
expected for a cervical strain of this severity. Treatment included manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home stretching
program instruction. Billing records reflect single entries for each service without duplicate or repeated charges. At the time of
this summary, the patient continues to report intermittent neck discomfort with activity, and a gradual return to normal function is
anticipated.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
